# FDG9040

> DO NOT invoke `Task.Wait()` or read the `Task.Result` property in an Async method; instead, use `await`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.2.5.3 Avoiding Deadlock.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1849
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

CA1849 reports Task.Wait() and the Result property of Task<TResult>, and other blocking calls that have an asynchronous variant, in methods that are async or return a task (probe with SDK 10.0.402). task.GetAwaiter().GetResult() is not reported, so coverage is partial. Replacing the call with await may make the method async; CA1849 has no code fix. FDG9041 shares CA1849.

## From the book

The `await` keyword causes the Task to yield, which allows other Tasks to continue. The `Task.Wait()` method—and the `Task.Result` property—instead do a blocking synchronous wait, which is inefficient and can lead to deadlock in some situations.
